filename: Hybrid modeling of evapotranspiration_ inferring stomatal and aerodynamic resistances using combined physics-based and machine learning.pdf
title: Hybrid modeling of evapotranspiration: inferring stomatal and aerodynamic resistances using combined physics-based and machine learning
parameterization_target: surface resistance (rs) and aerodynamic resistance (ra) within Penman–Monteith equation for latent heat flux (QLE) and sensible heat flux (QH)
code_availability: Processed data and analysis scripts are available from the corresponding author upon request, and the repository will be published together with this article. Data are openly available at 10.5281/zenodo.7078500.
testbed_rationale: Uses publicly accessible benchmark eddy covariance site data via Zenodo and demonstrates hybrid parameterization learning for intermediate land-surface resistances (rs and ra) embedded in physical flux equations.
pain_points: Equifinality/non-uniqueness when inferring multiple latent intermediate resistances simultaneously from a single target flux (QLE)
Physically implausible or uninterpretable intermediate variables when models are under-constrained
Energy balance closure problem in eddy covariance observations requiring correction filters and screening
Instability and observational noise amplification when inverting physical equations directly
extraction_notes: The paper uses the Penman-Monteith framework coupled with neural networks that estimate intermediate resistance variables. Two regularization approaches (theory-driven a priori constraint on aerodynamic resistance and data-driven multi-task learning predicting both QLE and QH) successfully resolve equifinality.
